commit_reviews.summary: The agent replaced a modular Blueprint-based multi-file Flask seed with a simpler single-file tasks API, keeping the SQLite idiom but dropping the seeded architecture and documentation.

problems: redundant ALTER TABLE owner_id inside init_db while CREATE TABLE already defines it
commit_reviews.summary: Adds JWT auth, password hashing, and per-user task ownership scoping that correctly thread owner_id through all queries and the auth decorator.

compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the seed's complete auth system (users/tokens/items/admin blueprints) and rebuilt a task manager from scratch, so Session 2 had to re-implement authentication entirely instead of building on the seed

Redundant migration code: init_db() creates the tasks table with owner_id already included, then runs a defensive 'ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN owner_id' in try/except — dead code that signals uncertain schema handling
Repository hygiene: __pycache__ .pyc files and the binary tasks.db were committed to git across both sessions
No requirements.txt or dependency manifest — jwt/werkzeug/flask availability was only checked ad-hoc via bash, hurting reproducibility

The multi-file seed was collapsed into a single monolithic app.py (~235 LOC), and pre-existing tasks from Session 1 have NULL owner_id (no backfill), leaving them invisible to all users after Session 2's isolation change
key_decisions: Greenfield rebuild in Session 1: replaced the multi-file Flask Auth API seed with a single-file SQLite task CRUD app
JWT-based auth (pyjwt HS256, 24h expiry) added in Session 2 as the feature addition, replacing the seed's custom token scheme
Per-user ownership model: tasks table gains owner_id FK and every read/update query is scoped by owner_id, enforcing data isolation
werkzeug password hashing (generate/check_password_hash) over the seed's salted-SHA256 approach
Idempotent schema bootstrap with app-context init_db() at import time plus defensive ALTER TABLE try/except
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the two sessions. Session 1 produced a clean, minimal CRUD task API with 18 passing tests, though it threw away the seed's auth machinery. Session 2 built directly on that single-file structure — same endpoints, same test fixtures — and layered on JWT authentication, a users table, per-owner task scoping, and cross-user isolation tests, growing coverage to 39 passing tests including 401s and ownership boundaries. The code remains a readable monolith with solid edge-case handling, though marred by the redundant owner_id migration and weak dependency/repo hygiene.
story_review.summary: A coherent two-session progression where a greenfield minimal task API was cleanly extended with JWT auth and per-user ownership (39/39 tests passing), at the cost of discarding the seed's existing auth and leaving minor schema and hygiene debt.
